### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7ebe4058895e0494541b29c7fcbbddd5efc4e0ab` — the merge of head `8f56596d3681d0eaec6220d6bb6cc8912ebc9ebc` into base `3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7ebe4058895e0494541b29c7fcbbddd5efc4e0ab && git checkout 7ebe4058895e0494541b29c7fcbbddd5efc4e0ab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac 8f56596d3681d0eaec6220d6bb6cc8912ebc9ebc && git checkout -B drift-repro 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac && git merge --no-ff 8f56596d3681d0eaec6220d6bb6cc8912ebc9ebc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3ee6af44fd6b91b339358fb6f805584b1d2a1aac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong. Verdicts in product words (#28534 class); mechanism detail for the two should-fixes is in a private note with the seat.

2. **The body seam** (`ObjectQL.registerApp`). The new pre-pass (`packageBodyObjectAndAppOwnerStampRefusal`) runs after the forward conversion and before `invalidateSummaryIndex`, `manifests.set`, the datasource index and `installPackage`, so a refused body leaves no package record, object or app. It walks `objects` in array form (by `name`) and name-keyed map form (by key, which the map branch assigns as `name`), every `apps[]` entry the loop would register (`name || id`, nameless skipped, the loop's own rule), and the manifest-as-app under exactly step 4's condition. The envelope is `collectionItemOwnerStampRefusal`'s (`VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, `issues[]` at `_packageId`). Through the install-local door that is 422 `PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` with the judge's message, no ledger entry. **Right.** An installed package's app or object carrying another package's owner stamp is now refused at the install, and nothing of the package registers.
3. **A nested plugin** (`registerPlugin`). The plugin's objects (array and map) and plugin-as-app are judged against the parent's id before the plugin's own registrations and outside the two `try` blocks that log and continue. **Right for the plugin's items.** But the top-level pre-pass does not walk `manifest.plugins[]`, and nested plugins register at step 7, so a refusal raised for a nested plugin lands after the parent body's record, objects, apps and collections are live. That is the same class as the dev's out-of-scope finding (a), reached through the same public door. **Should-fix S-b**, carried below; not a must-fix, because the refusal itself is right and the residue class pre-dates this PR.
4. **The residual door** (`registerUnclaimedTopLevelObjects`). Every residual object is judged against the residual's id before any registers, in the same envelope; residual apps were already judged by `registerUnclaimedTopLevelItems` (`RESIDUAL_TYPES_WITH_OWN_PATH` excludes `app`). With `apps` now judged at the body seam and the build door, the three doors agree on `apps`. **#28695 S2 is settled**, and the judge's docblock sentence S2 asked to correct is corrected.
5. **The build door** (`stack.zod.ts`). `applyCollectionItemOwnerStampGate` iterates the list over the parsed stack and over each `packages[]` body, arrays only; the stack schema declares `objects` and `apps` as arrays (`z.array(ObjectSchema)`, `z.array(AppSchema)`), so both are reached, issues at `objects.N._packageId` / `apps.N._packageId` with the judge's `build` words. No gate code changed; the list drives it. `plugins` stays `z.unknown()`, judged by the boot (item 3). **Right.** The build-side key-by-key pin (#28695 S3) is still not in spec; the objectql `collection-item-owner-stamp-doors.test.ts` walk holds the boot's refusals equal to the list over `STACK_DEFINITION_KEYS`, and with `objects` / `apps` added it is what pins both. Adequate for this PR; S3 stays on #28695.
6. **The metadata door** (`registerArtifactBodyCollections`). `artifactItemOwnerStampRefusal` judges every item of a judged collection, on both the container branch and the plain branch, before `applyProtection` and before the sink stores, in the engine's envelope. The collections are the build door's list intersected with `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE` (so `objects` and `apps` are judged here too, `objectExtensions` and `workflows` are not, consistently with the build door). Reached by the artifact door (which parses `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` first, so the build door judged it already) and by a config boot's residual through `AppPlugin` → `MetadataPlugin.registerUnclaimedTopLevel`, which no parse judges. **Right.** The order's "cover it with the same judge if it is reachable" is met.
7. **The boot path** (`loadMetadataFromService`). Unchanged but for a comment. It files `app` / `view` / `flow` / `hook` under each item's stored stamp, and holds no body to judge against. The package-shipped writer of those stamps is the metadata plugin's body registration (item 6), now judged; the other writers of items this seam reads are the host's own project files on the FS loaders and stored metadata rows, neither an installed package's body; the row side is seat 1's #28673 / PR #28734, as the PR body says. **The deviation holds**: on the unparsed and `strict: false` paths every route by which an installed package's item reaches a registry is judged (the body seam, the residual door, the metadata door). The `isArtifactBacked` claim is right: it answers from the registry's package stamp through `lookupArtifactItem`, so filing a synced item unstamped would make every package-shipped view, app, flow and hook look runtime-authored to the managed-content seal.
8. **The in-place-stamp exemption for apps** (`registerAppNotingStamp`). The intent is the collection loop's: a stamp a registration of this process wrote is not the body's claim. The collection and seed loops read the pre-stamp value before stamping; the three new apps call sites read it after `stampPackage` has already stamped, so the exemption is recorded only when the package has no version. Direction: stricter, never looser; the controls pass because the unit manifests carry no version, and no suite or dogfood flow re-registers an app under a second package. The PR body's sentence that the exemption covers a module constant re-registered under a second package over-claims by that much. **Should-fix S-a.**
9. **Controls.** From the tests as read (not re-run): an app or object stamping its own package, or nothing, installs 200 and lists under its own package; the host's apps list as at boot before and after; the uninstall stays keyed on the registering package and removes both; `objectExtensions` store as before at the metadata door; #28534's 28 collections are untouched (the loop and its test are unchanged). **Right.** The metadata-plugin mock change in `metadata.test.ts` spreads the real `@objectstack/spec/kernel` and narrows only the type registry, which is what lets the artifact door reach the judge under that suite.

Nothing else moves; the 28 collections, `objectExtensions`, `picklistExtensions` and the configuration keys are as they were.

Objects refused for parity: ① items 2, 4, 6; no first-party fixture relied on a foreign object stamp (objectql, metadata and spec suites and the full dogfood battery reported green by the dev; not re-run). Readings are on `498f5c70`, whose tree the dev reports identical to `83e32c91`; the three commits on the head carry the same file set and the net diff matches the report, so the readings stand for this head.
- **Dev's out-of-scope findings.** (a) A refusal raised inside the collection loop leaves the package record and the already-registered objects and apps live until restart. Pre-existing (#28534's loop), reachable through install-local, and now also the shape of ① item 3. It does not change this PR's verdict: the two collections this PR judges are refused before anything registers, and the PR adds no new residue of that class except the nested-plugin case, which is the same class. It does warrant a card: the dev filed none ("not measured through a public door"), but the door is install-local and the refusal there is public. **Should-fix S-b** asks the seat to file it, carrying the nested-plugin shape with it. (b) `loadMetadataFromService` reads stamps from FS project files and stored rows: seat 1's lane, noted, no action here.

- `packages/spec/src/kernel/collection-item-owner-stamp.ts`: holds. Two members added to a frozen list the gate and the metadata door both iterate; the docblock's door table and its "not judged" list are now true of the code (the residual door's `apps` judgement, which #28685's record flagged as the one place the boot was stricter, is no longer an exception).
